highlightAliases.old: PCV13 should be given first, with PPSV given at least 8 weeks later, per ACIP (p1690).Current practice (not the book): PCV15, PCV20 or PCV21 for adults ≥50; after PCV15 give PPSV23 one year later (8 weeks for certain conditions); no PPSV23 after PCV20/PCV21 — CDC, 2026.
highlightAliases.new: PCV13 should be given first, with PPSV given at least 8 weeks later, per ACIP (p1690).Current practice (not the book): prior vaccination determines the schedule: PCV15, PCV20 or PCV21 for adults ≥50 who never received a PCV or whose history is unknown; after PCV15 give PPSV23 if not previously administered, one year later (8 weeks for certain conditions); no PPSV23 after PCV20/PCV21 — CDC, 2026.

highlightAliases.old: HAP = onset >48 h after admission or within 10-14 days after a hospital discharge (p1681).
highlightAliases.new: Hospital-acquired pneumonia begins at least 48 h after admission and was not incubating on arrival; Hazzard also discusses recent discharge (10–14 days) as a healthcare exposure, which alone does not define HAP (p1681).

highlightAliases.old: SCAP severity score (Table 105-5, p1686): major criteria — pH <7.30 (13 pts), SBP <90 mm Hg (11 pts); minor criteria — confusion (5 pts), BUN >30 mg/dL (5 pts), RR >30 (9 pts), multilobar/bilateral CXR (5 pts), PaO2 <54 mm Hg or PaO2/FiO2 <250 (6 pts), age ≥80 (5 pts); risk — low 0-1 (<10 pts), intermediate 2 (10-19 pts), high 3-4 (>20 pts).
highlightAliases.new: SCAP severity score (Table 105-5, p1686): major criteria — pH <7.30 (13 pts), SBP <90 mm Hg (11 pts); minor criteria — confusion (5 pts), BUN >30 mg/dL (5 pts), RR >30 (9 pts), multilobar/bilateral CXR (5 pts), PaO2 <54 mm Hg or PaO2/FiO2 <250 (6 pts), age ≥80 (5 pts); risk — low 0-1 (<10 pts), intermediate 2 (10-19 pts), high 3-4 (20 points or more).

highlightAliases.old: SMART-COP score (Table 105-6, p1687): SBP <90 (2 pts), multilobar involvement (1 pt), albumin <3.5 g/dL (1 pt), RR age-adjusted (1 pt: <50y ≥25/min, ≥50y ≥30/min), tachycardia ≥125 (1 pt), confusion (1 pt), oxygenation age-adjusted (2 pts: <50y PaO2 <70 or SpO2 ≤93% or PaO2/FiO2 <333; ≥50y PaO2 <60 or SpO2 ≤90% or PaO2/FiO2 <250), pH <7.35 (2 pts); risk for needing vasopressor/intensive respiratory support — 0-2 low, 3-4 moderate, 5-6 high, ≥7 very high.
highlightAliases.new: SMART-COP score (Table 105-6, p1687): SBP <90 (2 pts), multilobar involvement (1 pt), albumin <3.5 g/dL (1 pt), RR age-adjusted (1 pt: ≤50y ≥25/min, >50y ≥30/min), tachycardia ≥125 (1 pt), confusion (1 pt), oxygenation age-adjusted (2 pts: ≤50y PaO2 <70 or SpO2 ≤93% or PaO2/FiO2 <333; >50y PaO2 <60 or SpO2 ≤90% or PaO2/FiO2 <250), pH <7.35 (2 pts); risk for needing vasopressor/intensive respiratory support — 0-2 low, 3-4 moderate, 5-6 high, ≥7 very high (Charles et al., Clin Infect Dis 2008; the original score places age 50 in the younger group).

highlightAliases.old: Standard latent-TB regimen: isoniazid 9 months; alternative rifampin 4 months; isoniazid + rifapentine 12 weeks also effective (p1694).
highlightAliases.new: For latent TB, short rifamycin-based regimens are preferred when suitable, including rifampin 4 months or isoniazid plus rifapentine 12 weeks; isoniazid 9 months is an alternative when rifamycins are unsuitable (p1694; NTCA/CDC latent tuberculosis treatment guideline, 2020).

highlightAliases.old: Drug-resistant TB varies with the resistance pattern; in general, multidrug-resistant TB needs 18-24 months with 4-5 active drugs guided by susceptibility (p1694).
highlightAliases.new: Drug-resistant TB varies with the resistance pattern; the book describes older 18–24 month regimens, but current guidance recommends six-month regimens for eligible adults with rifampin-resistant pulmonary TB, selected according to susceptibility and treatment history (p1694; ATS/CDC/ERS/IDSA guideline update, 2025).
